notes.title: Closed Beta Overview And More Tests?
notes.content:
Hey Manager!
[p align="justify"]This month we have dedicated our efforts to deliver a Closed Beta to players for for the first time. It was indeed our first rodeo and we have discovered new things to learn and improve on, with that being said we decided not to release a usual Dev Diary this month. Instead we want to take a look at the Closed Beta, and share some exciting news to come!  

The Closed Beta for Esport Manager: Road To Major was an opportunity for us to test the core mechanics of the game. The focus was on guiding a team through a full tournament cycle, giving players a taste of what it's like to manage an esports squad. You could either take control of one of 16 existing teams or create your own from an established roster core. 

[p align="justify"]A key component of the beta was the live match simulation. All matches were played on the map Inferno, where managers could influence the game directly by calling a timeout. You were given three timeouts per map, plus one for every overtime cycle, allowing you to choose from pre-defined tactics to counter your opponent's strategy. Beyond the tactical gameplay, the beta also featured a simple inbox system, where you'd receive a welcoming email and notifications about tournament teams and other vital information. 

[p align="justify"]We’re thrilled with the feedback we’ve received and are excited to announce that we will be hosting another Beta in a month. All of the players who tested the Closed Beta agreed on one thing, they see the vision of the game and they like it, that is exactly what we wanted to hear! This new Beta will introduce additional bugfixes, features and content, expanding on the core gameplay you've already experienced. Stay tuned for more details on how to participate and what new features you can expect to see!

notes.title: Dev Diary #5 – Tournaments and Events, Your Path to Glory
notes.content:
Hey Managers!


In Esport Manager: Road To Major, the very pulse of your team's journey beats within our dynamic Event System. These aren't just mere tournaments….they're the battlegrounds where legends are forged, where your strategic genius is tested, and where every victory pushes you closer to global dominance. Events are the core of competitive play, offering varied challenges and opportunities for your team to climb the ranks.



Your access to these high-stakes competitions is directly tied to your team's standing in the World Ranking. As your squad hones their skills and secures more victories, they'll ascend the ranks, unlocking invitations to increasingly prestigious tournaments. But be warned, invites for these coveted events will always come with a deadline, meaning that you have to reach the world rank in time before the Event starts!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45267012/482fe8c7fe101990783542563152c8c2169f8112.png"]

You'll need to act fast to secure your spot. Your team will always have a guaranteed slot in the lowest-tier events, providing a constant stream of opportunities to compete, refine tactics, and push towards higher echelons. Every match, every tournament, is a stepping stone on your path to glory!



We've meticulously structured the competitive landscape into distinct Event Tiers, each demanding unique strategies and showcasing different levels of prestige. You'll begin your journey in fierce Local LANs if you choose to start from the scratch, then ascend through C-Tier, B-Tier, A-Tier, S-Tier, and ultimately, the pinnacle of competitive play, the Majors. Each tier brings tougher opponents, larger prize pools, and greater glory, mirroring the real world progression of esports.


Diverse Tournament Formats
Prepare for an incredible array of tactical challenges! Our events feature a diverse range of Tournament Formats, designed to reflect the complexity and excitement of real-world esports. You'll encounter approximately 9 distinct group stage formats and around 12 unique playoff structures. This rich variety means every tournament demands a fresh approach, forcing you to adapt your roster, strategies, and even player mentalities to secure victory.



Navigating this bustling competitive world is made seamless through your Event Hub, which serves as your central command center. This intuitive interface is split into a detailed Event Listing on the left, showing upcoming and past tournaments with their names, logos, dates, locations, tiers, and prize pools. Powerful filters allow you to quickly pinpoint events based on their status, your team's registration, tier, or prize size.


Event Details
When you click on any event, you're transported to its dedicated detail page full of information designed for deep analysis. The Overview provides vital stats like dates, location, prize pool, and participating team count. The Participating Teams list reveals your opponent's names, ranks, and how they qualified, giving you crucial scouting data.



Track the live action with Recent Matches, showing match times, competing teams, and results. The Tournament Standings clearly display placements, prize shares and even highlight if your team's success unlocked a qualification to another event.



Finally, the Results Section lets you dissect every outcome. Dive into detailed Group Stage Tables (with expandable rows for complex formats like Swiss) or navigate the thrilling Playoff Bracket. Hover over any match to illuminate a team's path through the bracket, or click for a convenient Match Summary Pop-up with all the key details. Every piece of data is at your fingertips to help you strategize, adapt, and lead your team to esports glory!

notes.title: Dev Diary #4 – Financing Sponsors
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We're back with another dev diary for Esport Manager: Road To Major, and today let's discover a topic without which no professional esports team could function, sponsors! We know that financial management is key, which is why we've spent a lot of time ensuring the sponsorship system is realistic, deep, and full of interesting decisions.


How to Earn? Introducing "Marketability"
Money is the driving force behind every team, and sponsors are your primary source of income. But how do you attract the biggest and best deals? The key is your team's Marketability. This will be expressed as a percentage and visually represented by five stars (or ten half-stars).



What makes up Marketability?

World Ranking Position: The higher you are, the more attractive you are to sponsors. 

Every 5 positions in the top hundred earns you +2%.

Being in the Top 10 brings an additional +5%.

And reaching the Top 3 adds +5%! You can gain a maximum of 50% this way.



Individual Player Marketability: Your star players have their own value. The more popular and successful your players, the better for the entire team. This contributes a maximum of 30% to the team.

Facility and Staff Bonuses: Investing in your facilities and qualified staff pays off! These factors contribute the remaining 20% to your overall Marketability.



Each sponsor will offer you a contract with several key parameters: 

You can only get as good a deal as your marketability level is, this value can never exceed your current Marketability but it can go lower. It's up to you to improve your reputation and attract better deals!

Contract Duration: How long (months) the sponsor will collaborate with you.

Upfront Payment: An immediate financial injection. 

Monthly Payment: A stable income for your budget.

Bonus Payment: A one-time reward for achieving specific goals.

Sponsor Types and Their Offers

You will be able to have 1 main sponsor and 4 side sponsors.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45267012/e67bb7b3d6af207a7a3687de47c91c84423b31e1.png"]

Main Sponsor



The main sponsor will offer the longest and most beneficial contracts, usually ranging from 6 to 12 months. Their bonus offers will be ambitious but financially very attractive. For weaker teams, this could be qualifying for the Major, while for the best, it might be reaching the final stage of the Major tournament.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45267012/63714a5ef3204858634803ac644eaffb80f9243f.png"]

Other Sponsors

These partners will offer shorter contracts, typically 2 to 6 months, with smaller monthly payments. However, their bonus offers will be very interesting and strategically important, such as winning a certain number of matches, triumphing in an X-Tier tournament, reaching the finals or semifinals of an X-Tier tournament, or hitting a specific rank in the world standings.



Details That Delight!

To perfect the realism, we've implemented a system where sponsor logos will appear directly on your team's jerseys! Each style will have predefined positions, sizes, and rotations for logo placement.



What sponsorship goals would you set for your team first? Let us know!

notes.title: Dev Diary #3 – Mastering the Map Veto
notes.content:
Hey everyone!
Before any match kicks off, teams will engage in a crucial map veto (ban and pick) phase. The game will feature a pool of 7 maps for these strategic showdowns where banning and picking maps will be done using an intuitive drag-and-drop system.


How the Veto Works: Format by Format
The map selection process is determined by the match format:


Best of 1 (Bo1)
The objective is to narrow it down to a single decider map where you gotta know that you can outplay the opponent and secure the win, it is more about confidence than anything else!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45267012/44a4072ed00bc33f942094f24af28dbbb3d0d7b9.png"]

Team 1: Bans 1 map

Team 2: Bans 1 map

Team 2: Bans 1 map

Team 1: Bans 1 map

Team 1: Bans 1 map

Team 2: Bans 1 map

Decider: The last remaining map is played


Best of 3 (Bo3)
Teams pick their preferred maps and ban others, leading to a potential three-map series. Ban the one you do not know how to play or the one that the other team has been drilling and you would not stand a chance. Either way, make sure to pick the best one for you!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45267012/d8b7131620dbd7bcb1e2be810531cdb1ba9c2d7e.png"]

Team 1: Bans 1 map

Team 2: Bans 1 map

Team 1: Picks 1 map

Team 2: Picks 1 map

Team 1: Bans 1 map

Team 2: Bans 1 map

Decider: The last remaining map is played if needed.


Best of 5 (Bo5)
A more extensive selection process for longer series. This is about stamina, and endurance. It is going to take several hours and dedication to get this one home, but if anyone can do it, it might as well be you!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45267012/918b702f2990c359a2efcafe837d441e30a9110f.png"]

Team 1: Bans 1 map

Team 2: Bans 1 map

Team 1: Picks 1 map

Team 2: Picks 1 map

Team 1: Picks 1 map

Team 2: Picks 1 map

Decider: The last remaining map is played if needed.


Strategic Insights
To help you make informed decisions during the veto, the screen will display key statistics for each map, specific to each team and as we covered in previous dev diary, you will get some insights from your inbox as well to make you extra prepared. 

Winrate: Your team's success rate on that particular map.

Matches Played: The number of times your team has played on that map in the last 3 months.

notes.title: Dev Diary #2 - Inbox and Incidents
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Welcome back to the dev diary for Esport Manager: Road to Major! Today, we want to touch on two core mechanics that will shape your daily grind and challenge your decision-making skills: the constant flow of information via your Inbox and the unpredictable chaos of Incidents. Mastering these is key on your road to glory!

Never Miss a Beat: Your Inbox
Think of your Inbox as the nerve center of your entire operation. Being a successful manager means staying informed, and this is where everything crucial lands – from high-level strategy down to the nitty-gritty details. Forget digging through different menus; your Inbox is the central hub for vital communications from everyone who matters:

Your Inner Circle: Expect direct messages from your CEO outlining season goals or delivering performance reviews (good or bad!). Your trusty Assistant will ping you about expiring contracts, completed HQ upgrades, or potential scheduling clashes for tournaments. Your Coach will send detailed training reports, flag player fatigue issues, or let you know when a tactic is perfectly honed.

The Wider World: Analysts will drop detailed scouting reports on upcoming opponents right into your lap. Media outlets might offer interview opportunities, share juicy transfer gossip, or give you the lowdown on shifting world rankings and map pool changes. Even tournament organizers will slide in with those all-important invitations.

Staying on top of your Inbox, filtering the noise, and acting on crucial intel promptly will be vital for success. Miss a critical report or a contract deadline? That could be the difference between lifting a trophy and looking for a new job!

Expect the Unexpected: Incidents

But let's be real, managing an esports team isn't just about planning and execution. Sometimes, things go sideways. That's where Incidents come into play, throwing unexpected curveballs your way just when you think you have everything under control.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45267012/43fac123122e73fdc676bdaf632da32ea18d74f0.png
These aren't just background events, they demand your immediate attention. An Incident might pop up randomly, or be triggered by a previous decision or event in your game. When one hits, the game pauses, you must deal with it before moving forward.

You'll be presented with a scenario and typically 2-3 choices on how to respond. Do you back your star player after a public outburst, potentially damaging team reputation but boosting their loyalty? Do you accept a risky, last-minute sponsorship deal that could save your finances but comes with strings attached?

notes.title: Dev Diary #1 – The Start
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

welcome back to the dev diary for Esport Manager: Road to Major! Today, we want to pull back the curtain on what you can expect when you first launch the game and begin your journey to esports glory. Those initial choices are crucial, setting the tone and strategy for your entire managerial career.

Choose Your Origin
Right off the bat, you'll need to decide on your managerial background. We call these "Origins", and there are five distinct options to choose from when you start a new game. Think of an Origin as your unique starting advantage – a permanent boost that reflects your chosen specialty.

Maybe you're a former pro player known for inspiring locker room speeches, to give your team a natural morale boost. Or perhaps you're a financial mastermind, able to squeeze extra value out of every sponsorship deal. While the options provide specific bonuses, each one offers a meaningful nudge to your playthrough, encouraging different management styles right from the start. Choose wisely!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45267012/d9c83ed3e11e094dc55776e4acddc5bfc1e562ad.png

The Crossroads – Pick Your Path
Once you've selected your Origin, you face your first major strategic decision: how will you enter the competitive scene? There are two distinct routes:

Take the Helm of an Existing Team: jump straight into the action by taking control of an established organization. You'll likely inherit a decent roster, some existing infrastructure, and a more stable financial situation. Sounds good, right? The catch is the weight of expectation. The board, the fans, maybe even the star players – they have history and high demands. You'll need to deliver results quickly, or you might find yourself facing the CEO and potentially looking for a new job sooner than you think! It's a path filled with immediate pressure but also immediate potential.

Build From the Ground Up
Fancy yourself a true visionary? Then you can choose the challenging but rewarding path of creating your own esports organization from scratch. You'll start with limited funds, no players, and a huge mountain to climb. The early days will be tough, demanding smart recruitment and careful budget management. However, the payoff is complete control. Every victory, every trophy is purely down to your vision and hard work. And let's be honest, who doesn't want to design their own team identity? You'll get to customize your own jerseys with cool colors and emblems, creating a brand that's uniquely yours!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45267012/5653d48c104aa7185aed5e7ed432b2f49e254c8d.png

We're really excited about how these starting options shape the game. What do you think? Which path sounds more appealing to you right now? Let us know!

notes.title: Dev Diary #0 – The Vision
notes.content:
Hello everybody!

Today we would like to kick-off a series of Dev Diaries about our upcoming game Esport Manager: Road to Major. In these monthly blog posts, we will try to introduce individual features of the game and explain how they will work. This first entry will be about a general overview of the game and its vision.

So let’s get right into it. If we would describe the game in a single sentence for you it would probably be: “Less complex ‘football’ manager with First Person Shooter Esport teams”. Hopefully that sounds as good to you, as it sounded to us.

In the past, we've been working on two mobile racing games and for a long time we also wanted to make a game on Steam. So we started thinking, what would be the best genre for our first game on PC and we settled on a management focus game. Why did we go with the Esport FPS? Simply because all of us played and enjoyed their fair share of competitive shooter games, especially Counter-Strike, and we really liked the idea of bringing an esport into a classical sport based management game.

And very soon after that, we decided on main design goals for the game which are:

Authenticity – Being as close to the real experience of the esport organizations is the major focus of our game, giving you the opportunity to play within the realistic rules and tournaments.
Esport atmosphere – We very much enjoy watching professional players and teams competing against each other in thrilling matches and this is something we would like to get across with our match simulations.
Management focus – Hiring, financing, planning, training and developing of your team will be your bread-and-butter and we want you to be in control and make all the necessary decisions.

So this is all that we wanted to share with you this month. Please let us know what you think about it and how you like the idea. And if you’re interested in more information, feel free to join our Discord server and come back to us next month, when we should have a follow up post, in which we will introduce the first feature of the game!
